mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as financials and construction outperform.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle demand shock with sector rotation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 4% signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the previous year's average while PAYEMS grows below trend signals a shift from spending to saving, implying weaker consumer demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous year average AND PAYEMS < previous year trend for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) acceleration above 0.5% from the prior month while UNRATE remains below 3.5% signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average while GDPC1 grows below trend signals a housing-led demand recovery that benefits construction and related sectors, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average AND GDPC1 < trend for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
